advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that fails a fetch with a credentialed remote URL and asserts the raised WorkspaceError contains the role token (`<review remote>`) and NOT the URL/credential substring.
evidence: workspace.py:76-80: "def _fetch(root, role, url, ref): ... Errors name the remote's ``role``, not its URL, which may carry credentials." ... `_git_ok(root, "fetch", "--quiet", url, ref, shown=f"fetch --quiet <{role} remote> {ref}")`
test_network_fetch_stall_abort_851e.py:113-117 asserts only `pytest.raises(ws_mod.WorkspaceError)` on a failing fetch (url http://r.invalid/x.git) and never inspects the message for URL absence
ABSENCE: search_files for 'remote>' in tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py returned (no matches); no test anywhere asserts the credential/URL is redacted from the WorkspaceError
advisory.finding: The new credential-redaction behavior is untested: _fetch deliberately substitutes `shown="fetch --quiet <{role} remote> {ref}"` for the raw argv so the remote URL (which 'may carry credentials') never reaches the WorkspaceError, yet no test asserts the URL is absent from the raised error message. A fetch failure with a credentialed URL (e.g. review_remote_url='https://user:token@host/x.git') would still pass every existing test even if the redaction were reverted, because the fetch-failure tests only assert that WorkspaceError is raised (test_network_fetch_stall_abort_851e.py:114) or that it names the op/stall, never that the URL/token is excluded.
scenarios: A regression that reverts the `shown=` redaction leaks a credentialed fetch URL into the job's error payload, and CI stays green
An operator-configured review/tickets remote with an embedded token fails to fetch; the token lands in the surfaced error
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_opcert_service.py (or the fetch-stall module), fail a fetch via a factory/monkeypatch with cfg.review_remote_url='https://user:s3cr3t@host/x.git', assert pytest.raises(WorkspaceError), then assert 's3cr3t' not in str(exc) and '<review remote>' in str(exc).
